h: Making a day of it at Rock-a-Nore
p: The aquarium sits in one of the most characterful corners of Hastings, and it's worth giving yourself time to explore the area around it. The tall, black-painted net huts on the Stade are unique to Hastings, used for generations to store fishing gear, and they make a striking sight. The beach-launched fishing fleet still works from here, so you might see boats hauled up on the shingle.

Right on the doorstep you'll find the Fishermen's Museum, housed in an old church, with a historic fishing boat inside and plenty of stories about the town's seafaring life. The Shipwreck Museum is nearby too, packed with finds from wrecks along this stretch of coast. Both are a nice way to add a bit of local history to an aquarium visit.
How long do you need? The aquarium itself is a manageable visit of an hour or two, so it's easy to fit around everything else in the Old Town.

If you've got energy to spare, ride the East Hill Cliff Railway up to the Hastings Country Park for spectacular clifftop walks and sea views, or head the other way along the seafront to the West Hill, where the ruins of Hastings Castle look down over the town. Hastings Contemporary, the art gallery next to the net huts, is another great spot to pop into.
End the day with fish and chips from one of the many chippies in the Old Town, eaten on the beach as the sun goes down. It's a proper seaside day, the Hastings way.
